findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: agent-referee-mcp
findings.detail: 'agent-referee-mcp' launches agent-referee-mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["agent-referee-mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=0.99): sealed_review
findings.detail: The description of 'agent-referee-mcp.sealed_review' scores 0.99 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: injection_markers. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: injection_markers, entropy, log_len, imperative_density.

evidence.description: FREE OR PAID. Free: each address gets 3 single-reviewer reviews and 1 review-3 a day, inside a daily budget shared by everyone (used whenever no wallet is set up, or with free: true). Paid: $0.05, or $0.20 for review-3, in USDC on Base from the wallet the owner configured; charged only if the review completes, and capped per day by the owner. Multi-part (paid only, $0.60 for review-3x2, $0.70 for review-3x3): send the work as 2 or 3 pieces instead of one output, and three reviewers from three co

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
